prompt: Point $P$ is at $(4, 1)$. You move it $2$ units right and $3$ units up. Where is $P$ now? Write it like $(x,y)$.
hint: Each kind of move changes only one coordinate. Decide which coordinate a sideways move changes and which an upward move changes.

hints.text: Each kind of move changes only one coordinate. Decide which coordinate a sideways move changes and which an upward move changes.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Moving $(1,1)$ right 2 gives $(3,1)$. Then up 3 gives $(3,4)$. Same moves for $P$.
Moving right adds to $x$ and moving up adds to $y$. Starting from $(4, 1)$, work out $4 + 2$ and $1 + 3$.

explanation: Moving right makes the $x$-coordinate bigger, so add the $2$ units to it: $4 + 2 = 6$.
Moving up makes the $y$-coordinate bigger, so add the $3$ units to it: $1 + 3 = 4$.
Write the new $x$ first and the new $y$ second: $P$ lands on $(6, 4)$.
